text:
maria: Heads-up — profiler run after yesterday's adaptive-kernel-scoring rollout shows a tail-latency regression on short-seq requests (~8k p95->p99 increase). Grafana -> https://grafana.redwood/graph/s/abc123 :chart_with_upwards_trend:
aj: can you paste the query? which route?
maria: route=/api/generate, mixed seq length traffic. p95 up 12ms, p99 up 42ms. batch_size histogram shifted: MORE small batches. Snapshot -> https://grafana.redwood/d/hist/xyz
liam: hmm, is KV cache hitrate changing? small batches could be kv-cache churn
maria: kv_cache hitrate steady at 89%, but eviction_rate spiked 3x around the rollout window. logs show repeated cache invalidations by scorer: `kernel-scorer v2` flagged incompatible cache entries
zhen: that matches: adaptive scorer tags kernels with model-hash+seq-bucket, we changed tag format yesterday.
aj: oh, so cache keys mismatched => cache misses => longer token decode paths -> more kernel swaps -> tail
liam: can we revert the scorer tag change quickly? or make it backward-compatible
maria: propose revert on canary (deploy 1802346000) and run perf-bot profiler for 10m. also adding instrumentation: per-route kernel-switch count, per-token kernel-selection time
perf-bot: scheduled profiler run -> id: prof-1802345689, collecting: per-token latency, kernel_switch_count, batch_size_histogram
aj: also lower scheduler max-wait from 6ms -> 3ms to encourage larger batches for short-seq requests?
zhen: lowering max-wait reduces queueing but may reduce batching efficiency. Let's run A/B: canary with revert + unchanged scheduler, and canary2 with revert + max-wait=3ms
maria: agreed. can someone open a quick runbook with rollback steps + query links? i'll tag infra
liam: I'll open runbook and include `kubectl rollout undo deployment/kernel-scorer` steps and the tracer ids. Also will add a dashboard panel: token-latency breakdown by kernel and by batch-size.
aj: for next step, add alert: p99 token-latency increase > 20% over baseline for any route -> page oncall
maria: perfect. keeping notes here. Thanks :thumbsup:
